title: Fomo Kernel trigger-matrix attempt record (#458)
description: One line of a result file: the JSONL append-only log evals/triggers/run_triggers.py's `record` subcommand writes to and `score` folds and scores. The readable contract; run_triggers.py's read_result_file()/build_attempt() hold the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency (same posture as evals/episodes/episode.schema.json). Every field here is exactly what #458 asks a runner to record per attempt, plus ts and schema_version for the log's own bookkeeping.

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601 seconds, auto-stamped by `record` at write time (e.g. 2026-07-29T13:46:02Z). Informational only -- file order, not ts, is the ordering authority when folding repeated attempts for the same key (mirrors skills/fomo-kernel/tools/ux_receipt.py's stated precedent for its own append-only trace).

host.description: Free-form host id (e.g. claude_code, codex, antigravity). Not a closed enum on this record: HOSTS in run_triggers.py is only the default matrix `dry-run`/`score` report against, so a future host or an owner-approved second thin entry point can be recorded without editing the tool -- the same choice skills/fomo-kernel/tools/ux_receipt.py made for its own --client.

host_version.description: The host/CLI/app version string actually exercised.

model.description: The underlying model the host resolved to for this attempt, in the operator's own words (e.g. "Claude Opus 5", "GPT-5.6 Codex").

installed_skill_population.description: Skill/capability ids visible to the host at invocation time (per #273/#458: which skills could plausibly have competed for this trigger). May be an empty list on a host with no enumerable skill registry -- absence of a registry is not the same claim as an empty population, and the raw_outcome field is where that distinction should be spelled out if it matters to a specific attempt.

prompt_id.description: Must resolve against evals/triggers/corpus/<locale>/<split>.json. `record` looks this up itself; the caller never supplies expected_route or class directly, so an operator cannot record a self-contradictory expectation by mistyping a flag.

class.description: Derived from prompt_id via the corpus, not operator-supplied.

expected_route.description: Derived from class via EXPECTED_ROUTE_BY_CLASS, not operator-supplied: review_positive->review, pre_trade_positive->pre_trade, adjacent_negative->no_trigger.

actual_route.description: What actually happened, as the operator observed it. "no_trigger" also covers a host error, refusal, or otherwise broken response: from the user's perspective the fomo-kernel capability was not delivered either way, and the specifics belong in raw_outcome rather than a fourth ambiguous enum value.

raw_outcome.description: Free-text account of what the host actually did, in the operator's own words. Never empty -- the whole point of a per-attempt record is that a verdict is traceable to a description, not just a route label.
